2027-05-17.title: The Blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of the Church
readings: I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers (or: Acts 1:12–14, All these were constantly devoting themselves to prayer, together with Mary the mother of Jesus)
Glorious things are spoken of you, O city of God
Woman, here is your son. Here is your mother
2027-05-17.alt: Memorial, kept on the Monday after Pentecost since Pope Francis inscribed it in the General Roman Calendar (decree of the Congregation for Divine Worship, 11 February 2018). The readings of the memorial are proper and are used today in place of those of Monday of the Seventh Week in Ordinary Time (Sirach 1:1–10; Mark 9:14–29). In the first reading, Acts 1:12–14 may be read instead of Genesis. With the Easter season ended, Ordinary Time resumes today with the Seventh Week (Year I), and the Angelus replaces the Regina Caeli. Liturgical colour: white (from tomorrow, green).
2027-05-17.verse: When Jesus saw his mother and the disciple whom he loved standing beside her, he said to his mother, “Woman, here is your son.” Then he said to the disciple, “Here is your mother.”
theo: The day after Pentecost the Church turns to the one who was in the upper room when the Spirit came, and calls her by a name that sums up her place in God's plan: Mother of the Church. The first reading takes us back to the beginning, to the garden after the first sin. The Lord God calls: “Where are you?” Adam hides, afraid; he blames the woman, and the woman blames the serpent. Then God speaks to the serpent the first promise of salvation in the Bible, which the Fathers called the Protoevangelium, the first Gospel: “I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will strike your head, and you will strike his heel.” A woman and her offspring will stand against the power of evil, and the offspring will crush its head. The reading ends with a name: “The man named his wife Eve, because she was the mother of all living.” Christian tradition has seen in Mary the New Eve. St Irenaeus wrote (in substance) that the knot of Eve's disobedience was untied by Mary's obedience; what the virgin Eve bound by unbelief, the Virgin Mary loosed by faith. Eve became the mother of all the living in the order of nature; Mary, by her faith and her share in her Son's work, becomes the mother of all who live in grace. If Acts 1:12–14 is read instead, we see the apostles after the Ascension “constantly devoting themselves to prayer, together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus”: the Church at prayer, with the Mother in its midst. The Psalm sings of Zion, the mother city where every people is born: “Glorious things are spoken of you, O city of God,” and “All my springs are in you.”

The Gospel brings us to Calvary. “Standing near the cross of Jesus were his mother, and his mother's sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.” In the hour of his death Jesus looks at his mother and at the disciple whom he loved: “Woman, here is your son.” Then to the disciple: “Here is your mother.” “And from that hour the disciple took her into his own home.” He calls her “Woman,” as he did at Cana, the name that recalls the woman of Genesis. The beloved disciple is not named, so that every disciple can stand in his place. Jesus does not only provide for his widowed mother; from the cross he gives her as mother to all whom he loves, and gives them to her as children. Then, “knowing that all was now finished,” he says “I am thirsty,” and “It is finished,” and “gave up his spirit.” Finally a soldier pierces his side, “and at once blood and water came out.” The Fathers saw in that blood and water the sacraments of the Eucharist and Baptism, and the Church herself born from the side of Christ, as Eve was formed from the side of Adam. At the foot of the cross, Mary stands at the birth of the Church; in the upper room she prays at its Pentecost. St Paul VI solemnly declared her Mother of the Church on 21 November 1964, at the Second Vatican Council, on the day the Council approved its teaching on the Church, Lumen Gentium, whose last chapter is about her. St Augustine had written (in substance): Mary is the mother of the members of Christ, because by her love she cooperated so that the faithful might be born in the Church.
outline: Ask: who taught you your first prayer? For most of us it was a mother. Today the whole Church thanks God for her Mother.
Point 1 · The woman and her offspring
The first promise in Eden; Mary, the New Eve.
Jesus' gift from the cross to every beloved disciple.
The Church born from the pierced side, gathered with Mary in the upper room.
live: Give Mary a place in your home today: pray the Angelus at noon, the first time since Easter, or light a candle before her picture and pray one decade of the Rosary as a family.
Be a child of the Church
Do one thing today for your parish, your mother in faith: help a priest or sister, visit a sick parishioner, or simply thank someone who serves.
2027-05-17.prayer: O God, Father of mercies, whose Only Begotten Son, as he hung upon the Cross, chose the Blessed Virgin Mary, his Mother, to be our Mother also, grant, we pray, that with her loving help your Church may be more fruitful day by day and, exulting in the holiness of her children, may draw to her embrace all the families of the peoples. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Lord Jesus, from the cross you gave us your Mother; like the beloved disciple, we take her into our homes. Holy Mary, Mother of the Church, who prayed with the apostles for the Holy Spirit, pray for us now as we begin again the ordinary days of the year, that we may do whatever your Son tells us. Amen.
altar: From the pierced side of Christ came blood and water, and the Church has always seen there the sacraments that build her up: Baptism and the Eucharist. Mary stood by the cross when that blood was shed; at every Mass the same sacrifice is made present on the altar, and the Church, with Mary, stands beside it. In the Eucharistic Prayer we name her first among the saints: “the glorious ever-Virgin Mary, Mother of our God and Lord, Jesus Christ.”

quick: In Eden God promised that a woman and her offspring would stand against the serpent; the Fathers saw Mary as the New Eve.
From the cross Jesus gave his mother to the beloved disciple, and through him to every disciple: Here is your mother.
Since 2018 the Church keeps the Monday after Pentecost as the memorial of Mary, Mother of the Church; Ordinary Time resumes today.
2027-05-17.action: Pray the Angelus at noon today, for the first time since Easter, and offer it for your parish.
2027-05-17.question: Have I really taken Mary into my home, as the beloved disciple did?
kidsaint: When Jesus was dying on the cross, he looked at his mother Mary and at his friend John, and said to John: here is your mother. Jesus gave his own mother to John, and to all of us! Then after Jesus went to heaven, Mary prayed with the apostles until the Holy Spirit came. That is why we call her the Mother of the Church. Lesson: Mary is your mother too; you can talk to her any time, and she will lead you to Jesus.

family.explain: When Jesus was on the cross, his mother Mary was standing close by, with his friend John. Jesus said to Mary: here is your son. And to John: here is your mother. From that day John took Mary into his home. Jesus wants us to take Mary into our home too. She is the Mother of the whole Church, our family of faith.
family.intention: We pray for all mothers, especially mothers who are sick, alone or grieving, and for our parish family.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we make Mary feel at home in our family?” Pray the Angelus together at noon or in the evening.

illus: In many Kerala homes, when a daughter marries and leaves for her new house, her mother gives her a small picture of the Blessed Virgin to keep in the new prayer corner. It is a way of saying: you are going far from me, but you are not going without a mother. That is what Jesus did on the cross. He was leaving his disciples, and he did not leave them orphans: before he died, he gave them his own Mother.

pm.open: Holy Mary, Mother of God and Mother of the Church, you stood by the cross and prayed with the apostles for the Spirit. Pray with us now. Amen.
share: Where are you? (Genesis 3:9). Where am I hiding from God today, and what would it mean to answer him?
Here is your mother (John 19:27). What place does Mary have in my daily life and prayer?
All these were constantly devoting themselves to prayer, together with … Mary the mother of Jesus (Acts 1:14). How can our group pray more faithfully together, as the first Church did?
pm.resp: Glorious things are spoken of you, O city of God.
interc: For the Church, our Mother, that through Mary's prayers she may be fruitful in holiness and draw all peoples to Christ.
For the Pope and the bishops, that like the apostles in the upper room they may be united with Mary in prayer.
For mothers, especially those who suffer for their children or have lost them, that Mary may comfort them.
For those who feel orphaned or alone, that they may know they have a Mother in heaven and a family in the Church.
For our group, that as Ordinary Time begins we may live each ordinary day doing whatever Jesus tells us.
pm.close: Father, your Son gave us his Mother as he hung upon the cross. Through her prayers, make us faithful children of the Church. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, yesterday we celebrated Pentecost, the birthday of the Church. Today, the very next day, the Church turns to a mother. Every birth has a mother, and the Church does too. Since 2018 the Monday after Pentecost has been the memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of the Church.

The first reading takes us to the very beginning. After the first sin, God calls Adam: where are you? (Genesis 3:9). Adam hides and blames. But in the middle of that sad scene God makes a promise: I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will strike your head (Genesis 3:15). Long before Bethlehem, God already had a woman and her Son in mind. The Fathers called Mary the New Eve: what Eve lost by disobedience, Mary restored by her yes.

In the Gospel we stand at the cross. Jesus is dying. And with almost his last breath, he thinks of his mother and of his friend. Woman, here is your son. Here is your mother. And from that hour the disciple took her into his own home (John 19:26–27). The disciple has no name in the Gospel, so that you can put your name there. Jesus gives his Mother to you. And then from his pierced side flow blood and water, the sacraments by which the Church is born and fed. Mary was there.

And after the Ascension, Mary was in the upper room, praying with the apostles until the Spirit came (Acts 1:14). She is the Mother who stays with the Church in prayer. Today Ordinary Time begins again. Ordinary days, ordinary work, ordinary family life. Let us take Mary into our homes for these ordinary days, as John did. At noon today we pray the Angelus again; let us pray it with love. And let us listen to her one instruction, given at Cana: do whatever he tells you. Holy Mary, Mother of the Church, pray for us. Amen.
kids: Children, when Jesus was on the cross, his mother Mary was standing near him with his friend John. Jesus said to John: here is your mother! Jesus gave his own Mummy to John, and to you and me! Mary is the Mother of the whole Church. Whenever you are sad or scared, you can talk to her, and she will take you to Jesus. Let us say: Holy Mary, my Mother, pray for me!

concl: From Eden to Calvary to the upper room, God has placed a Mother at the heart of his plan of salvation.
Jesus gave her to us from the cross; she prayed with the apostles for the Spirit; she remains the Mother of the Church in its ordinary days.
